ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a uniform magnetic field of $\mathrm{B}=0.5\mathrm{T}$, there is a rectangular coil with $\mathfrak{n}=100$ turns and side lengths ${\mathrm{L}}_{1}=0.1\mathrm{m}$ and $L_{2}=0.2\mathrm{m}$. The coil starts rotating counterclockwise around the central axis $\mathrm{OO^{\prime}}$ at an angular velocity of $\omega=314\mathrm{rad/s}$ from the position shown in the figure.

1. What is the maximum induced electromotive force generated in the coil?
2. What is the effective value of the induced electromotive force in the coil?
3. What is the average value of the induced electromotive force as the coil rotates through $\frac{1}{4}$ of a circle?
4. What is the instantaneous value of the induced electromotive force when the coil rotates by $30^{\circ}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular coil abcd; the vertical dashed line OO' passes through the center of the coil, indicating the axis of rotation; multiple horizontal arrows point from left to right, indicating the direction of the uniform magnetic field B. The plane in which the rectangular coil lies is, at the initial position, in the plane of the figure together with these horizontal magnetic field lines, so the magnetic flux is 0 initially. The figure also marks the vertical side length L1 and the horizontal side length L2 of the coil, and has an arrow indicating counterclockwise rotation about the OO' axis. Reasoning: The coil area S=L1L2=0.1×0.2=0.02 m^2, number of turns N=100, magnetic induction intensity B=0.5 T, angular velocity ω=314 rad/s. According to the initial position given in the problem, after rotating through an angle θ=ωt, the flux linkage can be written as NΦ=NBS sinθ. From Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction e=-d(NΦ)/dt, the magnitude of the induced electromotive force is |e|=NBSω|cosθ|, so the maximum value Em=NBSω=100×0.5×0.02×314=314 V. The effective value Erms=Em/√2=314/√2=157√2 V. When rotating through 1/4 of a turn, θ goes from 0 to π/2, the change in flux linkage is NBS, and the time used is Δt=(π/2)/ω, so the magnitude of the average induced electromotive force e_avg=Δ(NΦ)/Δt=NBS/(π/(2ω))=2Em/π≈2×314/3.14=200 V. When rotating through 30°, the magnitude of the instantaneous value e=Em cos30°=314×√3/2=157√3 V.
